focus: Channel priority inverted this cycle by measurement, not taste: of the three agent-skill directories a human would actually try, two are dead and one is alive. ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills (77,833 stars, the obvious target) merged 0 of its last 50 closed PRs and its most recent merge was 2026-05-22 (145 days ago); travisvn/awesome-claude-skills (15,540 stars) merged 0 of its last 50 closed PRs, most recent merge 2026-01-07 (9 months). davepoon/buildwithclaude (3,673 stars) merged 45 of its last 100 closed PRs and 23 of its last 50, with merges today (2026-10-24 11:01) and 12 on 2026-10-23, only 7 PRs open, and a documented CONTRIBUTING.md contribution path plus automated validation + auto-deploy to buildwithclaude.com. Star count is therefore a negative predictor of channel throughput here; merge velocity is the predictor, and it inverts the ranking. buildwithclaude is also structurally cheaper than anything proposed before: its .claude-plugin/marketplace.json accepts EXTERNAL repos via source {source:'github', repo:'owner/repo'} (56 such entries) and git-subdir with a pinned sha (27 entries), so a contribution can be a single marketplace.json entry pointing at hypetopher/aicompany, no fork of our code and no files donated into their tree (precedent: merged PR #536 renhua changed exactly one file, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, +27 lines; #449 ad-angle-research was merged the same day it was opened, ~6h). Second new fact, measured live: root-level SKILL.md is discoverable, not just skills/<name>/SKILL.md - OLDyade/animated-sketch-diagram has SKILL.md at repo root with .claude-plugin/marketplace.json and IS indexed on skills.sh (oldyade/animated-sketch-diagram/animated-sketch-diagram, 13 installs), and I proved the mechanism with a scratch repo at /tmp/skilltest2 (root SKILL.md + .claude-plugin/marketplace.json): npx skills add . --list printed the skill with its description. Third, and this CORRECTS the previous cycle's plan: install telemetry does not reliably yield a listing. Upstream vercel-labs/skills #2564 (opened 2026-10-22, OPEN, 0 comments) reports a successful npx skills add that never got indexed; #2568 (2026-10-23, OPEN, 0 comments) shows a listed skill whose page renders 'No SKILL.md available' because the skill folder is too large. So last cycle's E3 (self-install, expect the 404 page to become 200) is an unreliable success metric - the honest metric is npx skills add --list returning exactly 1 skill with an intact description, because install-time discovery is proven even where web indexing is not. Also measured: npm name 'aicompany' is already taken by an unrelated publisher (AgenticCompany/company, 0.3.17), so npm is a blocked channel for us, not an option. Demand for the niche is real and quantified: skills.sh q=aicompany returns 69 listings (metixai-official/metix-skills/metix-company-search 33 installs, skills.volces.com/ai-company-* 2-4) and ours is absent (page 404, npx skills add hypetopher/aicompany --list = 'No skills found'); q=growth returns 100 listings with proven comparables at 4,358-10,875 installs each (okx-growth-competition 10,875, event-growth-strategy 4,900, developer-growth-analysis 4,358); q=openclaw returns 100 listings led by openclaw/openclaw/summarize at 22,604, so agent demand for OpenClaw-shaped skills is the exact demand we are built for. Risks, ranked: R1 execution, still the binding constraint - gh gist list = 0, ops_social_posts = 0, post_tweet steps lifetime = 0, write_content succeeded = 95, draft_tweet = 126, analyze = 778, drafts/ = 147 files, GitHub traffic 14-day views 0 / uniques 0, repo 0 stars / 0 forks / 0 watchers, pushed_at 2026-02-09, so a 21st analysis proposal does not move anything unless an artifact ships; R2 upstream indexing is flaky (both #2564 and #2568 open, unanswered, 0 comments) so no metric may depend on the web listing appearing; R3 our repo has no LICENSE, no description, no topics and no README headline (gh repo view: description null, topics [], license null), which is what a directory entry needs to render; R4 the working tree is dirty (11 modified files, +2,094/-46) and 2 commits ahead of origin, git push --dry-run origin main succeeds, and a secret scan of the pending diffs found only env var NAMES (SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY), no values - the push is safe but must be a scoped reviewable commit; R5 folder size: #2568 shows large skill folders render as 'No SKILL.md available', so our skill must stay small (one SKILL.md, no bundled corpus - the 943 corpus SKILL.md files live under corpus/ and artifacts/ and must stay untracked). Experiments, small and measurable: (E1) ship ONE skill as root SKILL.md plus a 1-file .claude-plugin/marketplace.json in our own repo, name + description frontmatter only, no product name, no internal ids, no corpus, as its own scoped commit - measured by npx skills add hypetopher/aicompany --list returning exactly 1 skill with the description intact; (E2) open ONE upstream PR to davepoon/buildwithclaude adding a single .claude-plugin/marketplace.json entry pointing at hypetopher/aicompany with source {source:'github', repo:'hypetopher/aicompany'} - measured by 1 PR opened, 0 PRs to ComposioHQ and 0 to travisvn this cycle (their measured merge rate is 0), and if merged, our entry live in their marketplace; (E3) publish the README headline plus repo description + topics + LICENSE (MIT) so both the GitHub page and any directory entry render a real description - measured by gh repo view returning a non-null description and topics count > 0, plus traffic uniques > 0 in 7d versus today's 14-day zero; (E4) the structural fix that lets E1-E3 run without a human in the loop: add a publish_skill-or-push step kind to EXECUTABLE_STEP_KINDS (src/services/proposal-service.ts:100, currently analyze|draft_tweet|write_content|post_tweet) and to the auto_approve policy allowed_step_kinds (currently draft_tweet, crawl, analyze, write_content - note 'crawl' is allowed there but is not an executable kind, a live mismatch) - a git push needs no new adapter because the token already carries repo scope and git push --dry-run origin main already succeeds - measured by one accepted publish step and one skill live without a manual shell command. Guardrails: no post_tweet, no ops_social_posts writes, no demand or reach claims from self-installs, no install-counter comparison across repos, no internal ids, paths or proposal numbers in anything published, no corpus or artifacts/ content staged, no new upstream issue, no npm publish under the taken name, exactly one upstream PR this cycle, and no analysis-only proposal until E1 and E2 have a measured outcome.
